_meta.description: Evidence-based Mini-PRS variant database for G×E Health Simulation Engine
_meta.important_note: All effect sizes are from published GWAS or meta-analyses in peer-reviewed journals. SNPs without GWAS-level quantitative confirmation are marked TODO_VERIFY in the effect_size_beta field. This database is for EDUCATIONAL SIMULATION only — NOT for clinical risk prediction.

variants.beta_unit: kg/m² BMI increase per risk allele
variants.trait_description: Body Mass Index (BMI) — continuous trait; obesity risk — dichotomous trait
variants.population: European (trans-ancestral meta-analysis, N=71,022; replication in East Asian and South Asian cohorts)
variants.source: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; Frayling et al. (2007) Science 316:889–894; Speliotes et al. (2010) Nat Genet 42:937–948
variants.functional_context: Intronic variant in FTO gene; regulates IRX3/IRX5 expression via long-range enhancer interaction affecting adipocyte thermogenesis (Claussnitzer et al. 2015, N Engl J Med 373:895–907)
variants.notes: Most replicated obesity-associated SNP in GWAS literature. Explains ~1% of BMI variance. Effect is on fat mass, not lean mass. Association visible from childhood onward.

variants.beta_unit: kg/m² BMI increase per risk allele
variants.source: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; in perfect LD (r²≈1.0) with rs1558902 in European populations; PMC7878711; PMC4260795
variants.functional_context: Functional causal variant at FTO locus. Disrupts ARID5B repressor binding, de-repressing IRX3/IRX5 and shifting adipocyte development from beige (thermogenic) to white (lipid-storing) — Claussnitzer et al. (2015) N Engl J Med 373:895–907
variants.notes: Considered the causal variant underlying the FTO obesity association signal. In near-perfect LD with rs9939609 in Europeans. Including both captures the primary FTO signal; their effects should NOT be summed (they tag the same haplotype). SE/OR marked TODO_VERIFY pending direct GWAS Catalog extraction.

variants.beta_unit: log-odds / liability scale for Alzheimer's disease
variants.trait_description: Late-onset Alzheimer's Disease (LOAD) — dichotomous diagnosis; also associated with amyloid-beta accumulation (PET imaging)
variants.population: European (Alzgene meta-analysis; multi-ethnic amyloid PET GWAS N=13,409; public AD GWAS summary statistics)
variants.source: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; Bertram et al. (2007) Alzgene meta-analysis; Ali et al. (2023) Acta Neuropathol Commun; Lambert et al. (2013) Nat Genet 45:1452–1458
variants.functional_context: Defines APOE ε4 allele (combined with rs7412). APOE4 protein is less efficient at clearing amyloid-beta from the brain and promotes neuroinflammation. ε4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease.
variants.notes: Per-allele OR ~3.7 (heterozygotes); ε4/ε4 homozygotes OR ~12–15. Effect is ancestry-dependent: strongest in Non-Hispanic Whites, weaker in East Asians. β=0.35 in amyloid PET GWAS. This SNP alone does not determine APOE genotype — must be interpreted together with rs7412.

variants.beta_unit: log-odds / liability scale for Alzheimer's disease (protective effect)
variants.trait_description: Late-onset Alzheimer's Disease — protective variant (reduces risk)
variants.population: European (Alzgene meta-analysis; public AD GWAS summary statistics)
variants.source: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; Bertram et al. (2007) Alzgene meta-analysis; Lambert et al. (2013) Nat Genet 45:1452–1458; PMC5944403
variants.functional_context: Defines APOE ε2 allele (combined with rs429358 genotype). APOE2 protein is more efficient at clearing amyloid-beta. ε2 is the strongest common protective variant for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. Negative beta indicates protective direction.
variants.notes: Together with rs429358, this SNP defines the APOE ε2/ε3/ε4 genotype. ε2/ε2 genotype is protective but associated with type III hyperlipoproteinemia (a separate trait with low population prevalence). Must NEVER be interpreted in isolation — APOE genotype is defined by the combination of rs429358 and rs7412 alleles.

variants.beta_unit: TODO_VERIFY — continuous sleep duration (hours) or chronotype score per allele
variants.trait_description: Chronotype (morningness-eveningness preference) and sleep duration; C allele consistently associated with evening chronotype across multiple candidate gene studies; interaction with short sleep on prediabetes risk (OR=2.11, 95% CI 1.39–3.18, Israeli cohort N=12,092)
variants.population: Multiple populations (Japanese N=421; Iranian N=403; Mediterranean N=1,495; Israeli N=12,092); candidate gene studies only — NO GWAS-level summary statistics available
variants.source: ClinVar/Ensembl for variant identity. Candidate gene studies: Mishima et al. (2005); PMC9161580 (2021); EPIC-Spain (PMC9739590). NOTE: rs1801260 has NOT reached genome-wide significance (p < 5×10⁻⁸) in any published GWAS of sleep duration or chronotype.
variants.functional_context: 3'-UTR variant (3111 T/C) in the Circadian Locomotor Output Cycles Kaput gene. CLOCK is a core circadian rhythm transcription factor forming a heterodimer with BMAL1 to drive expression of PER and CRY genes. The C allele may alter mRNA stability or translational efficiency, affecting circadian period length.
variants.notes: CRITICAL: This is the most studied CLOCK variant, but its association with sleep/chronotype is from candidate gene studies and has NOT been confirmed at genome-wide significance in UK Biobank or 23andMe GWAS meta-analyses (N > 450,000). Effect sizes therefore cannot be reliably quantified as a per-allele beta. For educational simulation purposes, a conservative estimate could be derived from the literature, but this should be marked as a model assumption, not a validated GWAS finding. The gene-level role of CLOCK in circadian biology is well-established mechanistically.

variants.population: European (GWAS Catalog; UK Biobank; Jones et al. 2019 Nat Commun 10:1585, N=697,828)
variants.source: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog. Jones SE et al. (2019) 'Genome-wide association analyses of chronotype in 697,828 individuals provides insights into circadian rhythms.' Nature Communications 10:1585. PMID: 30696823.
variants.functional_context: GWAS-identified chronotype locus near CLOCK gene. Reached genome-wide significance in the largest chronotype GWAS to date (Jones et al. 2019). Exact effect sizes pending direct GWAS Catalog extraction.
variants.notes: This SNP is included as a GWAS-validated chronotype locus in the CLOCK region. Unlike rs1801260, this variant reached genome-wide significance. However, exact beta/OR values, risk allele, and MAF require direct extraction from the GWAS Catalog entry (GCST007083 or related). All quantitative fields marked TODO_VERIFY pending that extraction.

variants.beta_unit: TODO_VERIFY — continuous trait (e.g., grip strength in kg, or athletic performance metric) per allele
variants.trait_description: Power/sprint athletic performance — case-control meta-analyses. R allele (C) associated with power athlete status (OR≈1.2). No significant association with grip strength or general-population muscle strength in GWAS.
variants.population: Multi-ethnic meta-analyses (El Ouali et al. 2024; Pabalan et al. 2019; Chelly et al. 2025). Strongest effect in Europeans; non-significant in African ancestry cohorts (4 studies, I²=0%).
variants.source: ClinVar/Ensembl for variant identity. Meta-analyses: El Ouali et al. (2024) Sports Med Open; Pabalan et al. (2019); Chelly et al. (2025) J Strength Cond Res. NOTE: This SNP has NOT shown significant association in large GWAS of hand grip strength or muscle strength in the general population (Willems et al.; UK Biobank).
variants.effect_type: additive (candidate gene meta-analyses; not GWAS-validated for general-population traits)
variants.functional_context: R577X nonsense polymorphism (C→T). The T allele (X) introduces a premature stop codon at position 577 (p.Arg577Ter), producing a non-functional α-actinin-3 protein. α-Actinin-3 is exclusively expressed in fast-twitch (type II) skeletal muscle fibers and is critical for explosive power generation. RR genotype = functional protein; XX genotype = complete absence of α-actinin-3.
variants.notes: CRITICAL: Despite being one of the best-known 'athletic genes,' ACTN3 rs1815739 has NOT shown GWAS-level significant association with muscle strength or grip strength in the general population. Its effects are primarily observed in elite athlete vs. control comparisons (case-control studies), not in population-level continuous traits. For an educational G×E simulation, the gene-level role of ACTN3 in muscle biology is well-established, but per-allele quantitative effects on health outcomes are unvalidated in GWAS. The OR≈1.21 is from meta-analyses of case-control studies, not GWAS. The effect_size_beta for a continuous health trait is marked TODO_VERIFY.

FTO.biological_confidence: HIGH — FTO locus is the strongest and most replicated common genetic association with BMI/obesity. Causal variant mechanism elucidated (Claussnitzer et al. 2015).
FTO.key_publication: Frayling TM et al. (2007) 'A common variant in the FTO gene is associated with body mass index and predisposes to childhood and adult obesity.' Science 316:889–894. PMID: 17434869.

APOE.biological_confidence: HIGH — APOE is the strongest and most replicated common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. ε4 increases risk; ε2 is protective. Mechanism involves amyloid-beta clearance and neuroinflammation.
APOE.key_publication: Lambert JC et al. (2013) 'Meta-analysis of 74,046 individuals identifies 11 new susceptibility loci for Alzheimer's disease.' Nat Genet 45:1452–1458. PMID: 24162737.

CLOCK.biological_confidence: HIGH — CLOCK is a core circadian rhythm gene with well-established molecular function (CLOCK-BMAL1 heterodimer). Genetic associations with sleep/chronotype are biologically plausible but individual SNP effects are weak and inconsistent.
CLOCK.key_publication: Jones SE et al. (2019) 'Genome-wide association analyses of chronotype in 697,828 individuals.' Nat Commun 10:1585. PMID: 30696823.

ACTN3.biological_confidence: HIGH — ACTN3 is a well-characterized gene with clear molecular function in fast-twitch muscle fibers. R577X nonsense polymorphism has documented functional consequence (loss of protein).
ACTN3.key_publication: El Ouali EM et al. (2024) 'A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of the Association Between ACTN3 R577X Genotypes and Performance in Endurance Versus Power Athletes and Non-athletes.' Sports Med Open. PMID: 38609671.
